clue.text: Flat belonging to a friend in which I wrote a short poem

indicators.note: the friend is the container in which the next pieces are written, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: Someone has written a little poem in a flat owned by a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belonging to a friend' sounds like possession, but the friend is a container; 'wrote' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained apartment, often on two floors, so it is a kind of flat.

clue.text: This is claimed to be remedial treatment

indicators.note: the word claimed is given rough handling, so its letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that this is a healing therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges CLAIMED; 'remedial' is the adjective that defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial care is curative, the job of a doctor, so it is medical in nature.

clue.text: An outlet for children

definitions.meaning: an outflow or exit point, as where a river discharges

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a way out or discharge, and a legal word for one's descendants.

clue.text: No atropine is used in this surgical procedure

parts.note: no means nothing, zero, the letter O

indicators.note: the drug and the nothing are used up as raw material, their letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A surgeon declares that this procedure goes ahead without the drug atropine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' gives O (nil), and 'is used' rearranges O plus ATROPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is the standard term for a surgeon's intervention on the body.

clue.text: Close to being miserly!

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of becoming a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nearby and, in an older sense, tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Apricot left to cook in a hot place

indicators.note: cooking alters what goes in, so the letters of apricot and L are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe says leave the apricot to cook somewhere warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical weather is that of the equatorial regions: sweltering and humid.

clue.text: Escape from a lady of French origin

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or get away from something.

clue.text: Witnesses where the cricket fan has been

definitions.text: where the cricket fan has been
definitions.meaning: a cricket fan has been ..., the five-day international matches

explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness formally; split, the letters say a fan was present at Test matches.

clue.text: In favour of leaving and giving up

parts.note: for means supporting
going means departing

explanation.surface: Someone supports departing and abandoning things.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgoing something means doing without it, renouncing it.

clue.text: Fellow who shows reckless disregard for road speed

indicators.note: showing no respect for the order of the words road speed, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man is described as a speed demon on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a dangerous man of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: Concerning a sailor who goes on strike

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a sailor
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A seaman walks out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: About is a preposition meaning regarding or on the subject of.

clue.text: Sounds as though this leader had a hold on his empire

indicators.note: the clue signals a word spoken, not spelt

parts.words: had a hold on his empire
parts.note: one who grabbed and held power is a seizer

explanation.surface: A ruler's grip on his realm is the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman name is said like 'seizer', one who seizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, hence any autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Distances travelled by Gisela and me

indicators.note: the letters of Gisela and me go on a journey and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes how far they and Gisela have driven.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileages are numbers of miles covered, i.e. lengths of journeys.

clue.text: Admits to causing someone to be involved

definitions.meaning: as in letting someone in for trouble, landing them with it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both allows inside and, with 'for', drags a person into an obligation.

clue.text: There are difficulties with using foreign currency in a back street

indicators.note: the money sits inside the turned abbreviation for street
back means the abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian unit of money

explanation.surface: Changing foreign money in a back alley brings problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a dodgy money-changer in an alley; 'back' is a reversal signal, not an adjective for the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles are problems or worries.

clue.text: Pole who catches up on contracts

parts.note: a bar is a rod or pole
gains on means closes the gap

explanation.surface: A Polish man is closing in on business agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement between parties, a deal.

clue.text: Waggon Lily decorated brilliantly without a note

indicators.note: decorating rearranges how things look, so these letters are reordered
without means one letter of waggon is dropped

parts.note: A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Lily has dressed up a cart splendidly, minus one note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A from WAGGON, giving WGGON; 'decorated' rearranges that with LILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowingly means radiantly, or with warm enthusiastic praise.

clue.text: Tends the slopes

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means is disposed towards; the noun means gradients.

clue.text: Making mock of Carol who has a foot problem

indicators.note: the singer has the foot complaint within, holding it inside

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol with sore feet is jeering at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name, but it is the verb sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorning someone means treating them with contempt, deriding them.

clue.text: Ruin the salesmen who return carrying trophy

indicators.note: the sales staff hold the prize inside them
return means the word for salesmen is read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
a cup is a sports trophy

explanation.surface: Salespeople coming back with an award are spoiling things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who return' works only on the salesmen, giving SPER before the trophy goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, like sinking a ship.

clue.text: Yearn for the Queen to have more time

parts.note: long for means yearn for
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone wishes the monarch could have extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying for a greater duration is staying for more time.

clue.text: One who takes it easy about the puzzle

parts.note: re means concerning
a poser is a tricky question

explanation.surface: Someone relaxing is mulling over a brain-teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reposes is resting, relaxing.

clue.text: This could get held up in bad weather

definitions.text: This could get held up in bad weather

parts.words: This could get held up in bad weather
parts.note: sounds like a delay from storms, but it is the rain shield raised over one's head

explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is carried aloft to keep off rain.

clue.text: Salts might watch races here

parts.note: salts are sailors, but also a bath salt named after a Surrey town whose downs host the Derby horse race

explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town gives its name both to magnesium sulphate salts and to the Derby racecourse.

clue.text: Come to a conclusion but feel nervous about it

definitions.meaning: to have the ... is British slang for being scared

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to finish; 'get the wind up' is a British idiom for getting frightened.

clue.text: First thing do it over again

indicators.note: over suggests turning things around, so the letters are reworked
first means just the opening letter of thing

explanation.surface: The first task is to do it once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes T from 'thing'; 'over' rearranges T plus DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same thing repeated, as said before.

clue.text: Little girl and I went in the night before

indicators.note: the I enters the day before, placed inside it

parts.note: eve is the evening before a festival

explanation.surface: A small girl and I entered on the previous evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Evie is a girl's name, a pet form of Eve or Evelyn.

clue.text: Returned to drop off skins

indicators.note: returned means the word for nodding off is read backwards

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep

explanation.surface: Someone came back to leave off some fruit rinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Peels are the outer rinds of fruit.

clue.text: Steers first violin through a seating plan

indicators.note: the letter passes through, sitting inside the rearranged seats
a plan lays things out afresh, so the letters of a seating are rearranged
first means just the opening letter of violin

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader finds a way through the seating chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' rearranges A SEATING, 'first' takes V from violin, and 'through' puts V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to direct a course, to steer.

clue.text: If you'll try my routes you won't know where you'll end up!

definitions.text: If you'll try my routes you won't know where you'll end up!

indicators.text: you won't know where you'll end up
indicators.note: the letters of try my routes end up in an unpredictable order

explanation.surface: A tour guide warns that his routes are unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you won't know where you'll end up' rearranges TRY MY ROUTES, and the whole clue describes the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach trip with a secret destination leaves passengers guessing until arrival.
